Penguin Explorer

exploredata is an R package containing prepared Palmer penguin data, a summary function, and an interactive Shiny app.

Intended user and question

This app is designed for undergraduate biology students learning about differences in body size among penguin species.

Question: How do body mass and flipper length differ among Adelie, Chinstrap and Gentoo penguins, and how do these comparisons change when viewing males and females separately?

Installation

Install the package from GitHub:

# Run once if remotes is not installed:
install.packages("remotes")

remotes::install_github(
  "ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-jlii0673-coder"
)

Launch the app 

library(exploredata)
launch_app()

The app runs locally and uses data included in the installed package. It does not download data when launched.

Using the app

  1. Select the species you want to compare.
  2. Choose All, Male or Female.
  3. Compare the scatterplot and summary table.
  4. Switch between sexes to investigate whether the species differences remain visible.

Each point represents one penguin. The horizontal axis shows flipper length in millimetres; the vertical axis shows body mass in grams. Colour identifies species.

The summary table reports selected, complete and excluded record counts, together with mean body mass and mean flipper length. Both means use records with both measurements available.

All includes records with unknown sex. Selecting Male or Female excludes records with unknown sex.

If no species are selected, the app asks you to select at least one.

Summary function 

summarise_penguins(penguin_data)

summarise_penguins() calculates sample counts and mean measurements by species. The app uses this exported function to generate its summary table.

Data and reproducibility

The source is palmerpenguins::penguins_raw, containing 344 records. The prepared dataset retains species, island, sex, flipper length and body mass.

The script data-raw/prepare_penguins.R selects and renames fields, standardises sex labels, retains missing values, checks the data, and saves data/penguin_data.rda.

To reproduce the prepared data, install the preparation tools and run the script from the repository root:

install.packages(c("palmerpenguins", "dplyr", "usethis"))
source("data-raw/prepare_penguins.R")

Data were collected and made available by Dr Kristen Gorman and Palmer Station LTER. The source data are distributed under CC0.

Source and citation information: https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/

Horst AM, Hill AP, Gorman KB (2020). palmerpenguins: Palmer Archipelago (Antarctica) penguin data. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.3960218

Interpretation and limitations

In the complete sample, Gentoo penguins have greater mean body mass and mean flipper length than the other two species. Use the sex filter to investigate whether this pattern is also visible within males and females.

Group means do not describe all individual variation. Compare the scatterplot as well as the table, and consider the unequal sample sizes and excluded records.

These data describe sampled penguins in the Palmer Archipelago. They do not necessarily represent all penguin populations. Observed associations do not establish causal relationships.
